description: AI-assisted editorial scenario model using the retrieved 31 October evidence snapshot. Factor scores are judgments, not measured quantities. Null factors use the neutral 0.5 prior. No score is a probability or an estimate of harm prevented.

factors.readiness: Maturity of the authority and operational route: 0 speculative; 0.5 identifiable instrument with missing adoption; 1 exact safeguard operating. Existing programmes do not establish exact adoption.
factors.timing: Room to implement the proposed safeguard by June 2027: 0 known to miss; 0.5 unresolved schedule; 1 demonstrated short execution path. Guidance or a pilot is not full deployment.
factors.coordination: Manageability of necessary dependencies: 0 numerous unresolved cross-border approvals; 0.5 several dependencies; 1 one empowered operational owner. Not a count of assumed vetoes or observed consent.
factors.reach: Potential governed activity if adopted: 0 single narrow trial; 0.5 programme or sector cohort; 1 broad frontier-model or infrastructure exposure. Ordinal editorial scope assessment, not a share of a common denominator.
factors.relevance: Strength of the proposed causal link to meaningful AI safety: 0 indirect administrative benefit; 0.5 plausible evidence improvement; 1 direct prevention or containment of a specified serious failure. Cross-domain valuation is an explicit judgment.
factors.remedy: Ability to act on failures if adopted: 0 advice alone; 0.5 review/escalation; 1 demonstrated binding hold and successful retest for this safeguard. Existing statutory powers are not proof of this outcome.

routes.xBasis: Draft contract and decision owners are identifiable, but setup can take 18 months after signature; a protocol is more plausible by Geneva than operating capacity.
routes.yBasis: Seven-project design envelope suggests broad infrastructure reach. Incident duties and termination are relevant, but tenant/model coverage and actual governed capacity remain unproven.

routes.xBasis: Executed programme contracts and recorded release-approval authority support readiness; the planned March award/April use leaves a plausible pre-Geneva path.
routes.yBasis: 100,000 access-enabled officials establish programme scale, not active use. A version-specific release gate is plausible; the exact supplier remedy is still missing.

routes.xBasis: National procurement precedents exist, but shared terms still require acceptance by three national systems.
routes.yBasis: A joint purchasing profile could spread evidence requirements across programmes. A matched procurement pool and shared enforceable remedy are not established.

routes.xBasis: GovTech already documents test, remediation and retest; a bounded deployment gate has fewer dependencies than a new international instrument.
routes.yBasis: Observed attack tests show a direct leakage mechanism, but known-attack retest is not held-out safety. Governed production exposure remains unknown; scope is assessed as a bounded deployment.

routes.xBasis: Two institutes have run independent evaluation pipelines; Japanese acceptance and common execution/scoring rules remain unresolved.
routes.yBasis: Reproducibility work could improve evidence across jurisdictions, but a shared evaluation result is not itself a deployment hold.

routes.xBasis: The equity announcement offers a possible negotiating window. A prior signed contribution is a different instrument; subscription terms and tranche timing are undisclosed.
routes.yBasis: A developer-level covenant could reach a broad model programme, but affected operations and binding equity rights are unknown. Financing totals are not safety coverage.

routes.xBasis: An operating award programme has review and suspension terms. The current application window has closed; a lawful next-cycle change remains necessary.
routes.yBasis: 196 award entries identify a programme population, not compute consumed. Conditional access could enforce evidence duties if incorporated into applicable terms.

routes.xBasis: Filed amendment machinery exists, but lender weights, borrower agreement and a genuinely discretionary new-credit event remain unresolved.
routes.yBasis: A frontier-developer covenant has potentially broad relevance. Existing committed credit is not discretionary leverage; safety rights and affected operations are unknown.

routes.xBasis: Monthly review and short terms-change notice offer an actionable route; Belgian/CSC authority and recipient acceptance still need confirmation.
routes.yBasis: Belgium's 7.4% LUMI envelope is a bounded potential scope, not protected use. An access appendix could connect evidence duties to allocation conditions.

routes.xBasis: Existing access processes can review some requests within weeks; adding evaluation rights requires EuroHPC, operator and recipient agreement.
routes.yBasis: The central allocation channel offers broader scope than one national share. Historical AI-labelled awards demonstrate activity, not adoption of the proposed evaluation condition.

routes.xBasis: Fast national review and a shared utilisation policy are precedents, but harmonisation across national channels adds dependencies; channel count is not a veto count.
routes.yBasis: National channels collectively hold half the allocation envelope. Common evidence terms could scale within LUMI; deduplicated usage and authority remain unresolved.

routes.xBasis: An in-house control tool is already operating with public replay inputs; one operational owner offers a tractable path to an authorised fallback exercise.
routes.yBasis: Fallback directly addresses a critical-service failure. Grid-wide control-energy totals do not establish model-controlled exposure, so scope is kept bounded.

routes.xBasis: A technical sandbox is decided, but its 12-month learning cycle extends beyond Geneva; a bounded interim exercise is more plausible than completed assurance.
routes.yBasis: Energy control is safety-relevant, but no named operational case or affected-asset inventory establishes the eventual reach and hold mechanism.

routes.xBasis: Spring guidance and prior supervisory interventions create a plausible pathway; deployer uptake and delegated ownership are still needed.
routes.yBasis: Accountability requirements may affect multiple developers, but guidance alone does not verify unauthorised-action prevention or a binding release gate.

routes.xBasis: An existing three-month testing programme and historical deployer/tester pairs provide execution precedent; purchaser authority must be added.
routes.yBasis: A purchaser hold can make testing consequential in a bounded cohort. Applications and industries represented are not completed gates or governed usage.

routes.xBasis: The Act and Decree identify an instrument, but final incident notices and a named covered operator remain unlocated; the rehearsal schedule is unresolved.
routes.yBasis: High-capability eligibility makes the route potentially relevant to serious AI risks. Eligibility thresholds do not identify actual covered operations or successful remedies.

routes.xBasis: An adopted AI programme and active inspection cases establish authority and activity. Long historical sanctions and the June 30 programme marker weaken pre-Geneva completion.
routes.yBasis: 23 active football-club facial-recognition cases provide a concrete cohort. An inspection can demand correction, but a technical retest and verified processing scope remain missing.

routes.xBasis: A 30-business-day assessment procedure exists; the current signing unit and operational handoff are unresolved.
routes.yBasis: No AI deployment population was recovered. Recommendations are nonbinding, weakening the proposed gate unless an internal hold is agreed.

routes.xBasis: Planned staffing and an unresolved postponement bill make commencement and implementation uncertain by Geneva.
routes.yBasis: A public AI survey identifies candidate institutions, not eligible high-risk systems. Exact operational assessment and remedy authority remain unresolved.

routes.xBasis: Existing supervisory activity supports an institutional route; AI-specific case duration and continued staffing are unknown.
routes.yBasis: Privacy retest could make corrective action verifiable. General caseload and the regulator's own policy-review tool do not establish governed AI exposure.

routes.xBasis: Prior-authorisation procedures have explicit investigation clocks. The selected linkage and data-holder rights must first qualify under the instrument.
routes.yBasis: A biometric-office footprint suggests a bounded service population. Offices are not eligible operations; the exact hold and retest still need agreement.

routes.xBasis: The recovered statute, sign-offs and historical reviewed DPIAs support an operational route. The 60-day lead time is not a final approval guarantee.
routes.yBasis: Biometric processing is a concrete safety/privacy mechanism, but historical reported users are not a verified current governed cohort; reach uses the neutral prior.

routes.xBasis: A March filing cycle and actual audit approvals offer a near-term amendment opportunity involving regulator, controller and auditor.
routes.yBasis: Technology-sector audit entries suggest potential programme reach, but no AI flag or accepted technical annex proves model coverage or corrective retest.

routes.xBasis: Controller and DPO roles exist in law, but the DPIA form and review register remain inaccessible. Breach clocks cannot estimate assessment duration.
routes.yBasis: No selected high-risk workflow or accepted retest was recovered. Registration counts and startup numbers cannot establish scope or an enforceable remedy.

routes.xBasis: An operating review and post-paid subsidy programme provides a decision point. Applicable exceptions and authority to add safety conditions remain to be resolved.
routes.yBasis: 303 project records demonstrate substantial programme activity. Linking evidence duties to future subsidy could be consequential, but allocations are not consumption or governed payments.

routes.xBasis: A four-stage accelerator names independent assurance; current delivery dates and signed acceptance authority are missing.
routes.yBasis: The entity/use-case pipeline suggests programme scope, not deployed agents. Independent assurance is relevant, but actual rollback rights are unknown.

routes.xBasis: Agreed testing plans and monthly reports provide a mechanism, but admission, preparation and 6–9 months of testing can exceed the Geneva horizon.
routes.yBasis: Completed product cohorts support a bounded sandbox scope. AI eligibility, exposed transactions and the specific agreed stop rule remain unresolved.

routes.xBasis: Existing consortium contracts and quarterly monitoring support a work-package route, but multiple signatories and a still-changeable contract are needed.
routes.yBasis: 23 supported consortia provide a programme-scale anchor with conflicting cumulative totals. Ordinary project failure does not automatically provide a safety clawback.

routes.xBasis: The named agency has performed security assessments, but those are not DPIAs; controlling scope and the exact release workflow remain unresolved.
routes.yBasis: One named AI licensing-system candidate keeps scope narrow. A specific release hold and processing inventory have not been recovered.

routes.xBasis: DPIA guidance assigns management responsibility, but no selected controller or dated implementation record supplies execution timing.
routes.yBasis: Thresholds define potential eligibility rather than actual governed deployments. Residual-risk acceptance is weaker than an enforceable hold and retest.

routes.xBasis: Historical LLM pilots exist; separate sandbox completions often exceed the available time and are only analogues, not a calibrated AIGPC schedule.
routes.yBasis: Three historical LLM cases support a narrow starting scope. Actual new-cohort rules and deployment-stop authority remain unknown.

routes.xBasis: The deploying agency head has an identified assessment role. Some transition markers precede Geneva and others follow it; qualifying system selection is essential.
routes.yBasis: Impact forms require users and scale, but no completed eligible deployment inventory was recovered. A named approval path suggests a possible gate, not observed enforcement.
